public_rationale: In February 2024, Marcus wrote that imagining perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots by that time the next year was 'bonkers'. A public leaderboard updated on 28 February 2025 measured hallucinations when models summarize documents: the best-scoring model, Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash, hallucinated in 0.7% of summaries, and no listed model scored zero.
limitations: The leaderboard measures one task, summarizing given documents, with an evaluation model built by Vectara, the company that publishes it.
The update is dated 28 February 2025, five days after the one-year mark.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: By about February 2025, one year after the post, there will be no perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots.

from_speaker: Imagining perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots by this time next year is bonkers
the passage replies to hopes that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) would fix hallucinations, calling that 'a six-month project' 'naive'
our_interpretation: We read 'bonkers' as a firm expectation that such chatbots would not exist by then.
We read 'by this time next year' as about 23 February 2025, and 'perfectly reliable, hallucination-free' literally: no measurable hallucination.
criteria.support_condition: An independent measurement from around February 2025 shows that leading chatbots available by then still hallucinated at a measurable rate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independent measurement from around February 2025 shows a chatbot available by then that did not hallucinate at all.
